svg.text: FRCS Part 1 (General Surgery) · sheet 2 of 2 · phaeochromocytoma · Conn's · Cushing's · adrenocortical carcinoma
Paroxysmal hypertension with the triad of episodic Headache, Sweating and Palpitations; pallor, anxiety.
Plasma free (or 24-h urinary) metanephrines; then CT / MRI + functional MIBG or 68Ga-DOTATATE.
~40% germline — MEN2 (RET), VHL, NF1, SDHx; SDHB carries higher malignant / extra-adrenal risk.
~10% bilateral, ~10% extra-adrenal (paraganglioma), ~10% malignant, ~10% familial (an underestimate today).
NEVER beta-block first — blocking β-vasodilatation leaves unopposed α-vasoconstriction and can precipitate a hypertensive
The commonest surgically-correctable cause of secondary hypertension; bilateral idiopathic hyperplasia is actually the commonest subtype,
Pituitary adenoma = Cushing's DISEASE (~70%); ectopic ACTH (small-cell lung, carcinoid)
Adrenal adenoma or carcinoma; bilateral nodular hyperplasia
Iatrogenic glucocorticoids — the commonest cause overall
Large (>4–6 cm), rapidly growing; often functional — Cushing's ± virilisation from androgens.
Heterogeneous, irregular margins, high unenhanced HU (>20), slow contrast washout, necrosis / calcification.
OPEN adrenalectomy with en-bloc resection — NOT laparoscopic; never percutaneous biopsy (seeding). Adjuvant mitotane; overall
Laparoscopic adrenalectomy is the gold standard for benign functioning tumours and small masses; convert to OPEN for large tumours
Treat the source — pituitary / adrenal / ectopic
In phaeochromocytoma, alpha-block BEFORE beta-block — beta-blockade first leaves unopposed alpha vasoconstriction and a
~40% of phaeochromocytomas are hereditary — offer genetic testing (MEN2, VHL, NF1, SDHx); SDHB carries the highest
Conn's needs adrenal vein sampling before surgery — CT can mislead, and only lateralised (unilateral) disease benefits from
In Cushing's, measure ACTH only AFTER confirming cortisol excess — suppressed ACTH points to the adrenal; non-suppressed
Suspected adrenocortical carcinoma → open adrenalectomy, never a percutaneous biopsy (seeding) — and always exclude a
Sources: Endocrine Society guidelines (phaeochromocytoma & paraganglioma; primary aldosteronism; Cushing's syndrome) · ESE/ENSAT adrenocortical carcinoma guideline · standard
ARR = aldosterone-renin ratio; AVS = adrenal vein sampling; ACC = adrenocortical carcinoma. Adrenal anatomy, physiology and the incidentaloma work-up are on sheet 1 of 2.
